diagnostic_evidence.quote: with the core tensor $\boldsymbol{\beta}^0 \in \mathbb{R}^{r_1^0 \times r_2^0 \times r_3^0}$. Then the initial tensor ${\bf V}$ takes the form of a rank ${\bf r}^0=(r_1^0,r_2^0,r_3^0)$ orthogonal Tucker representation
where $\{ {\bf v}_{\nu_{\ell}}^{(\ell)}\}_{\nu_{\ell} = 1}^{r_{\ell}} \in \mathbb{R}^{n_{\ell}}$ is the set of orthonormal vectors for $\ell = 1, \cdots, d$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proposition's statement is correct, but the proof's displayed verification is mathematically impossible as written: $V^{(\ell)}G^{(\ell)}$ is $n_\ell \times r_\ell^0$ with $r_\ell^0 < n_\ell$, so $V^{(\ell)}G^{(\ell)}[G^{(\ell)}]^T[V^{(\ell)}]^T$ has rank at most $r_\ell^0$ and cannot equal $I_{n_\ell}$. Orthogonality of Tucker factors means orthonormal columns, i.e. $(V^{(\ell)}G^{(\ell)})^T(V^{(\ell)}G^{(\ell)}) = G^{(\ell)T}V^{(\ell)T}V^{(\ell)}G^{(\ell)} = G^{(\ell)T}G^{(\ell)} = I_{r_\ell^0}$, which is what the proof actually needs to show.

failure_location.quote: proves the orthogonality  $V^{(\ell)} G^{(\ell)} [G^{(\ell)}]^T [V^{(\ell)}]^T =I_{n_\ell}$, which completes the proof.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false identity by the column-orthonormality computation $(V^{(\ell)}G^{(\ell)})^T(V^{(\ell)}G^{(\ell)}) = G^{(\ell)T}G^{(\ell)} = I_{r_\ell^0}$ using $V^{(\ell)T}V^{(\ell)}=I$ and $G^{(\ell)T}G^{(\ell)}=I$; no other change to the proposition or its uses is needed.
issues.overall_effect: The conversion of the two-level hybrid Tucker format to the standard Tucker format stands, but its proof does not establish the claimed orthogonality as written; the displayed identity is false and must be repaired for the proof to be valid.
issues.title: False orthogonality identity in the proof of prop:hybrid2Tuck
issues.why_classification: The result is true and only the final verification step is wrong; the repair is one line with no loss of content and no dependent claim changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $\| \boldsymbol{\xi} \|_1 = \sum_{k=1}^{R} |\xi_k|$ is the $\ell_1$ norm of the normalization constants.

issues.failure_explanation: The canonical weights $\xi_k$ in eq:func_val_cp are unrestricted real scalars, but the proof bounds $|\sum_k \xi_k(\cdots)| \leq \sum_k \xi_k |\cdots|$, which is valid only when $\xi_k \geq 0$. The lemma's first stated inequality has right-hand side $\sum_k \xi_k \times (\text{positive terms})$, which is false whenever some $\xi_k < 0$ (e.g. $R=1$, $\xi_1=-1$ makes the right side negative while the left side is nonnegative). The final 'in particular' bound using $\|\boldsymbol{\xi}\|_1$ is correct once $|\xi_k|$ is used throughout.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert absolute values: replace $\xi_k$ by $|\xi_k|$ in the first inequality of lem:ftilde-F and in the two proof chains; the final $\|\boldsymbol{\xi}\|_1$ bound is then valid as stated and thm:added-1 and cor:added-1 need no change.
issues.overall_effect: The first inequality of lem:ftilde-F and its proof are invalid for signed CP weights; the corrected final bound (eq:func_cp_error) and its users (thm:added-1, cor:added-1), which use only the $\|\boldsymbol{\xi}\|_1$ form, remain valid.
issues.title: Signed CP weights \xi_k handled without absolute values in lem:ftilde-F
issues.why_classification: A single-character repair restores the proof; the 'in particular' bound already uses $\|\boldsymbol{\xi}\|_1$ and all results built on it are unaffected, so no substantive claim is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The desired result then follows from the standard error analysis of the RHOSVD truncation \cite[Theorem 2.5]{khoromskij2009multigrid}.
and the singular values $\sigma_k^{(\ell)}$ are available after the SVD decomposition of the side matrices in the CP format.

issues.failure_explanation: The cited RHOSVD error theorem (Theorem 2.5 of khoromskij2009multigrid) applies to canonical tensors whose factors have unit $\ell_2$ norm, but the Chebyshev-coefficient CP vectors ${\bf c}_k^{(\ell)} = W^{(\ell)} {\bf q}_k^{(\ell)}$ are spline value vectors at $m_\ell$ nodes, not unit vectors ($W^{(\ell)}$ scales by roughly $1/\sqrt{m_\ell}$ and $\|{\bf q}_k^{(\ell)}\|_2 \approx \sqrt{m_\ell/n_\ell}$). Hence the factor $\|\boldsymbol{\xi}\|_2$ alone does not follow from the cited theorem; the norms $\|{\bf c}_k^{(\ell)}\|_2$ must be absorbed into the coefficients. As stated the bound is unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Normalize the coefficient vectors, $\tilde{\bf c}_k^{(\ell)} = {\bf c}_k^{(\ell)}/\|{\bf c}_k^{(\ell)}\|_2$, and replace $\|\boldsymbol{\xi}\|_2$ by $(\sum_k \xi_k^2 \prod_\ell \|{\bf c}_k^{(\ell)}\|_2^2)^{1/2}$ in lem:ftilde-fhat (and correspondingly in thm:added-1); the singular values are then those of the normalized side matrices. The form, rate, and computability of the bound are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The RHOSVD truncation term of lem:ftilde-fhat, and hence the second term of thm:added-1, is not justified as stated; after normalization the same bound holds with a computable modified coefficient norm, so the advertised error control is preserved up to a computable factor.
issues.title: RHOSVD error bound applied to non-normalized Chebyshev-coefficient CP vectors in lem:ftilde-fhat
issues.why_classification: The gap is a missing normalization hypothesis in an invoked theorem; the repair (absorb $\|{\bf c}_k^{(\ell)}\|_2$ into the coefficients) is a routine local step that keeps the bound's form and rate, changing only a computable constant.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For the algebraic cases, we first claim that the cost of evaluating a cubic spline interpolation at $m$ points given data on uniform $n$-point grid is $\mathcal{O}(m+n)$. Indeed, the computation of the spline coefficients requires solving a tri-diagonal system of size $4n-4$, which costs $\mathcal{O}(n)$, and the evaluation of the spline at $m$ points costs $\mathcal{O}(m)$ in case the $n$-point grid is uniform. Similarly, the cost of trivariate cubic spline interpolation which is required in \cref{alg:cheb_tuck_alg} is $\mathcal{O}(m^3(m+n))$.
Cheap and fast Tucker-ALS rank optimization for the small $ m\times m \times m$ coefficient tensor with $m \ll n$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof estimates the trivariate spline cost as $\mathcal{O}(m^3(m+n))$ by treating the univariate $\mathcal{O}(m+n)$ cost (construction $\mathcal{O}(n)$ plus evaluation $\mathcal{O}(m)$) as if it were incurred per evaluation point. In fact the spline is constructed once: solving the tridiagonal systems along all $3n^2$ grid lines costs $\mathcal{O}(n^3)$ (merely reading the $n^3$ data points already costs $\mathcal{O}(n^3)$), and evaluation at $m^3$ points costs $\mathcal{O}(m^3)$. The stated bound therefore omits $\mathcal{O}(n^3)$ and underestimates the true cost whenever $n^3 > m^3(m+n)$, i.e. for $n \gg m^{1.5}$ — precisely the advertised mesh-free regime $m \ll n$.

failure_location.quote: \cref{alg:cheb_tuck_alg}: $C_4 m^3(m+n) + C_5 m^3 + C_1 m^3 \log m + C_2 m^4 + C_3 m^4 |\log \varepsilon|$.\

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the spline term as $\mathcal{O}(n^3 + m^3)$ (construction plus evaluation), i.e. replace $C_4 m^3(m+n)$ by $C_4 n^3 + C_5 m^3$ in the complexity of alg:cheb_tuck_alg; the algorithm and the estimates for the other three variants are unchanged, but the headline complexity of this variant in the regime $m \ll n$ must be corrected.
issues.overall_effect: The complexity estimate for alg:cheb_tuck_alg in prop:compl is wrong in the regime $n \gg m^{1.5}$, in particular in the paper's key regime $m \ll n$: it omits the $\mathcal{O}(n^3)$ spline construction cost and can fall below it. The efficiency claim for the full-spline algebraic variant is affected; the estimates for the other three algorithms are intact.
issues.title: Trivariate spline complexity of alg:cheb_tuck_alg underestimated: O(m^3(m+n)) instead of O(n^3+m^3)
issues.why_classification: The correction replaces the headline complexity term of one of the four advertised algorithms and is not a typo — the stated bound is asymptotically too small in the paper's key regime $m \ll n$. The repair is contained ($\mathcal{O}(n^3+m^3)$) and the algorithm and other estimates survive, but a substantive quantitative claim must be weakened.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then the short-range part ${\bf P}_{R_s}$ is a highly localized tensor which has very small support and can thus be stored sparsely (see \cite{benner2018range} for details), while the ChebTuck approximation can be gainfully applied to the long-range part ${\bf P}_{R_l}$.

We can see that canonical vectors representing the long-range behavior of the Newton kernel, i.e., ${\bf p}_1, \cdots, {\bf p}_{15}$ can be well approximated by low-degree Chebyshev interpolants (left), while for short-range canonical vectors, the convergence is much slower (middle).
We can see that in this case, only when $m\gg n$ the ChebTuck approximation can give satisfactory results, which is not practical and does not reduce the storage cost.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper's own convergence analysis establishes that the low-index canonical vectors ${\bf p}_1,\dots,{\bf p}_{15}$ of the Newton-kernel CP tensor are the smooth long-range ones and the higher-index vectors are the localized short-range ones. The displayed split therefore assigns the long-range vectors to ${\bf P}_{R_s}$ and the singular short-range vectors to ${\bf P}_{R_l}$, contradicting the very next claims that ${\bf P}_{R_s}$ is highly localized and that the ChebTuck approximation works well on ${\bf P}_{R_l}$ — the paper shows ChebTuck fails on exactly those singular vectors. The reported success on the 'long-range part' (tab:lr_single_newton_error) is consistent only with the swapped split.

failure_location.quote: {\bf P}_{R_s} = \sum_{k=1}^{R_s} {\bf p}_k \otimes {\bf p}_k \otimes {\bf p}_k, \quad {\bf P}_{R_l} = \sum_{k=R_s+1}^{R} {\bf p}_k \otimes {\bf p}_k \otimes {\bf p}_k.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Swap the two summation ranges in eqn:Split_Tens, defining ${\bf P}_{R_l} = \sum_{k=1}^{R_l} {\bf p}_k^{\otimes 3}$ (long-range, smooth) and ${\bf P}_{R_s} = \sum_{k=R_l+1}^{R} {\bf p}_k^{\otimes 3}$ (short-range, localized); this single change makes the localization claim, the ChebTuck success claim, and all subsequent numerics valid as written.
issues.overall_effect: The range-separated splitting of the Newton-kernel CP tensor is defined with the long- and short-range index ranges interchanged relative to the paper's own canonical-vector analysis, so the claims that ${\bf P}_{R_s}$ is highly localized and that ChebTuck succeeds on ${\bf P}_{R_l}$ are false as written; all downstream ChebTuck results on the 'long-range part' (single kernel and multi-particle) are consistent only after swapping the two sums.
issues.title: Long-/short-range summation ranges swapped in the Newton-kernel range split (eqn:Split_Tens)
issues.why_classification: The source itself fixes the unique one-line repair (swap the two sums, since ${\bf p}_1,\dots,{\bf p}_{15}$ are established to be the long-range vectors); every substantive claim, including all reported numerical results, survives the swap, so no mathematical content is lost.
